sections.context: Flick is 2.3k lines and about to absorb Hammerspoon, Hyperkey, an app manager, a herdr client, activity tracking, tasks and an agent bridge. Today every feature leaks into three shared places: the closed `search::Action` enum (every feature adds a variant), `app::State` (every feature adds fields and match arms in enter/refresh/render/activate), and `config::Config` (every feature adds top-level keys). Objective-C/unsafe code is spread across app.rs, ui.rs, windows.rs, spaces.rs. Each new feature would make all of these shallower and more entangled (APOSD: change amplification, cognitive load, information leakage). This refactor makes features deep, independent modules behind a narrow interface, isolates the platform, and adds a text interface (socket + CLI) so other programs and agents can compose with Flick (Unix philosophy).
sections.behavior_invariant: Everything a user can do today works identically: (1) all hotkeys in an existing config.toml (hotkey, desktop_toggle, windows_hotkey, [window_keys]) bind and behave the same, including repeat-to-cycle halves; (2) existing config.toml files parse unchanged — new per-module sections are additive, old top-level keys remain valid; (3) launcher ranking is unchanged: same fuzzy matching, same frecency, and item ids `app:<path>`, `window:<title>`, `quicklink:<name>`, `builtin:<title>` are preserved byte-for-byte so the `usage` table in an existing flick.db keeps its history; (4) clipboard history keeps its 500-clip cap, dedupe, concealed/transient skip, and paste-into-previous-app; existing `clips` rows survive; (5) window switcher order (previous window first, other-desktop apps collapsed) and desktop toggle behave the same; (6) `flick snapshot <png> [query]` and `flick import-raycast <file>` keep their arguments, output and exit codes; (7) single-instance check, Accessory activation policy, and no network access remain; (8) idle CPU stays ~0 and the release binary stays under 5 MB.
sections.approach:
Layered single crate, boundaries enforced by a check script (split into a cargo workspace only if compile times or boundary violations demand it).

Layout:
- `src/platform/` — the ONLY place with `unsafe`, objc2, Carbon, AX, CG, CF. Exposes safe, Flick-shaped functions (pasteboard, workspace, ax windows, spaces, hotkeys, timers, panel). Deep module: callers never see CF types or selectors.
- `src/core/` — pure Rust, no platform imports where avoidable: `Item`, `Ranker`/frecency, `Event`, `Module` trait, registry, `Store` (shared SQLite + per-module migrations), config loading, control protocol types. Unit-testable without AppKit.
- `src/modules/<name>/` — one directory per feature: apps, quicklinks, clipboard, windows (snap), switcher, desktop, flick (builtins). Modules depend on core + platform, never on each other.
- `src/ui/` — the panel view; renders a `ListView` and forwards keys. Knows nothing about features.
- `src/cli/` — argument parsing and the socket client.

Key interfaces (keep them small; push complexity down):
- `trait Module { fn id(&self) -> &'static str; fn items(&mut self, cx) -> Vec<Item> /* root search contributions */; fn open(&mut self, view, cx) -> Option<ListView> /* own list modes */; fn activate(&mut self, key: &str, cx) -> Outcome; fn on_event(&mut self, ev: &Event, cx) {} ; fn command(&mut self, args: &[String], cx) -> Result<String> {} /* socket/CLI verbs */ }`. Default methods do nothing, so a module implements only what it needs.
- `Item { id: ItemId { module, key }, title, subtitle, accessory, icon, keywords }` — no Action enum; activation routes to the owning module by id. `Outcome = Hide | Stay(status) | Push(ListView) | Pop`.
- `Event` enum (AppActivated, PasteboardChanged, Wake, Idle(secs), DisplaysChanged, Hotkey(binding), ...) produced by platform observers and dispatched synchronously on the main thread; background threads post to main via a channel + main-queue wakeup. No polling except where macOS forces it (pasteboard changeCount).
- Config: each module deserializes its own `[<module>]` table (with `enabled`), so module config types are private to the module. Legacy top-level keys are mapped in one place.
- Store: one connection; each module declares migrations keyed by module name in a `schema_versions` table. Modules own their tables; no cross-module SQL.
- Control socket: `~/Library/Application Support/Flick/flick.sock`, one request per line (`<module> <verb> [args...]` as JSON array), one JSON reply. `flick <module> <verb> ...` prints plain text, `--json` prints raw. `flick events` streams events as JSON lines for composition with other tools.
- Errors: one small `Error` type in core; modules surface errors as status text, never panic. Each module's event/command handlers are wrapped so a failure in one cannot take the launcher down.

Order: gates and characterization tests first, then move code without changing it (platform), then change interfaces one at a time, porting one module per step.

steps.title: Quality gates: Rust check:all (fmt, clippy pedantic subset, test, custom checks) + CI + pre-commit
Characterization tests: item ids, legacy config parsing, store schema, window rect math
Move all unsafe/objc2/CF/AX/Carbon code into src/platform with safe APIs; boundary check forbids unsafe elsewhere
Core types: ItemId-routed Item, Outcome, ListView, Module trait, registry; delete search::Action
Port features to src/modules: apps, quicklinks, clipboard, windows, switcher, desktop, flick builtins; app.rs becomes a thin view controller
Per-module config tables with enabled flag; legacy top-level keys mapped in one place
Store: shared connection, per-module migrations via schema_versions; existing usage/clips tables adopted
Event bus: platform observers (app activated, pasteboard, wake, displays, idle) dispatched to modules on main thread; panic isolation per handler
Control socket + CLI client: flick <module> <verb>, --json, flick events stream; fold snapshot/import-raycast into the same dispatcher
Docs: ARCHITECTURE.md (layers, module contract, how to add a module), CLAUDE.md conventions, mulch records

acceptance: Characterization tests from step 2 pass unchanged at every later step.
An existing ~/.config/flick/config.toml and flick.db load with no edits; frecency order for a fixed query matches pre-refactor.
`flick snapshot out.png ''` and `flick snapshot out.png vsc` produce visually identical PNGs before and after.
Boundary checks pass: `unsafe`/objc2 only under src/platform; no `crate::modules::` imports inside another module; no `crate::platform` imports in src/core.
Adding a toy module touches only src/modules/<toy>/ plus one registry line (verified by doing it in the docs step).
Manual smoke test on the installed app: launcher, quicklink keyword, clipboard paste, window switcher, snap + cycle, desktop toggle, reload config.
Release binary < 5 MB; idle CPU ~0% over 60 s in Activity Monitor.
